newsitem.title: USA: Neuromedical PAPNET tests esophageal cancer.
newsitem.headline: Neuromedical PAPNET tests esophageal cancer.

text.p: Neuromedical Systems, Inc said on Wednesday a study showed its computerized screen to test for cervical cancer could also detect cancerous and pre-cancerous cells of the esophagus on smears.

In an study released at a U.S. and Canadian Academy of Pathology meeting, Neuromedical's PAPNET Testing System, normally used to sight abnormal cervical cells, was shown to facilitate early detection of esophageal cancer, it said.
The study was conducted by Leopold Koss of the Montefiore Medical Center in New York and other physicians. Koss was a consultant to the company, it said.

PAPNET tested 138 esophageal smears using its system of neural network and algorithmic technology, and correctly identified all 36 patients in the study who were positive or suspicious for cancer, the company said.

Investigators using the PAPNET system identified all types of carcinoma, such as squamous and adenocarcinomas of the esophagus and stomach, using the same neural network that was initially trained to detect cervical cellular abnormalities.

"The PAPNET test offers a new and intriguing option of improved diagnostic performance in esophageal cytology that may prove to be particularly valuable in mass screening for carcinoma of this organ, as currently practiced in China," Koss said.
In 1996, there were an estimated 12,300 cases of esophageal cancer and 11,200 deaths from the disease in the United States, the company said.
